name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +21 Republican partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Ezell running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Republican win at 97%
model.rationale: The district's heavy Republican lean, Ezell's incumbency, and his roughly 34-to-1 fundraising advantage over Jeffrey Hulum leave the Democrat with no visible path. Markets price a Republican win at 97%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any unexpected incumbent scandal or major outside spending against Ezell would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: South Mississippi's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Mike Ezell is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. His Democratic challenger, Jeffrey Hulum III, has run a minimal campaign, raising under $30,000 and reporting only a few thousand dollars on hand. An independent, Carl Boyanton, is also on the ballot but has shown little fundraising strength.
